request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: Throttle channel ch[2] pinned at minimum from t=88 s with throttle 0%, while attitude control stayed normal.
result.explanation: ch[2] follows throttle all flight, so it is probably the propulsion output. It dropped from 1.46e3 to 1.1e3 us and throttle fell to 0% at t=88 s. Whether this was commanded or a fault is not separable here.

evidence.shows: ch[2] steps to 1100 us and throttle to 0% within 1 s, from 46% and about 1.46e3 us at t=87 s
ch[2] stays flat at 1100 us and throttle at 0% until the end of the log, with altitude down to 5.75 m
Earlier low-throttle moments also drove ch[2] low, so ch[2] follows throttle (probably the motor channel)

checked.check: ch[2] versus throttle across the flight
checked.result: ch[2] falls whenever throttle falls (t=2-8, 20-30, 66-70). It is the only channel pinned flat at 1100 us after t=88.
Roll follows the 44 deg setpoint with about 1 s lag (t=89-91, t=103-105). Pitch and yaw also follow. Surface channels 1, 3, 4 and 5 keep moving normally.
Airspeed holds at 12-18 m/s. Altitude falls from 51 m to 5.75 m, about 2.5 m/s descent, which fits an unpowered glide or a landing approach.

effects.shows: Yaw and roll setpoints keep changing after the throttle cut, so the controller still tracks them
The altitude loss follows from zero thrust

next_action.action: Check the flight mode and throttle command around t=88 s
next_action.why: This settles whether the throttle cut was a commanded landing or failsafe, or an output or ESC fault.
how: Inspect mode and mission state history near t=88 s
Compare the throttle command with the ch[2] PWM output
Review ESC telemetry and the failsafe log

outcomes.label: Landing or failsafe commanded the cut
Throttle command stayed high but ch[2] fell
outcomes.means: Output or actuator fault on ch[2]

unknowns: Whether the t=88 s throttle cut was commanded
What the t=0 battery and sensor events refer to

hypotheses.claim: The propulsion output on ch[2] failed or was cut to minimum at t=88 s.
hypotheses.because: ch[2] and throttle step to minimum together and stay flat for 19 s.

hypotheses.claim: The attitude controller lost authority or failed.
hypotheses.because: Attitude follows its setpoints throughout, including after t=88 s.

hypotheses.claim: A landing or failsafe command, not a fault, set throttle to 0%.
hypotheses.because: Steady descent and a flat command are consistent with an intentional cut, but no mode data is present.
